messages.text: I’ll trace the cache lifetimes and invalidation path, then check what the profile exposes for timings, cache layers, operators, and completion proofs. I’ll keep this read-only and won’t build or run benchmarks.

The public profile contract already distinguishes request-core timings from end-to-end latency and reports several reusable cache layers. I’m following those fields into the executor now, especially to determine which caches survive requests and which are invalidated by edits.

I found no general cross-request cache for the final `CodeQueryResult`; its seed and relation memo tables are rebuilt per request. There are reusable lower-level stores, plus specialized durable type-flow root projections, so a repeated “warm query” can mean several distinct things. I’m checking the benchmark harness and edit/update paths to pin down those distinctions and the A→B→A case.
